transcript.text: Let’s start by checking if your dishwasher is receiving power at all. When you press the power button, do any lights or the display come on?
No, nothing at all. No lights, no display, totally dead.

Thanks for letting us know about the lights being out. Please ensure the dishwasher’s plug is fully inserted and that the socket or switched spur (often located above the worktop) is turned on. You can also try plugging in another appliance to see if it works there. If you suspect an electrical trip, do not keep resetting it. For your safety, only check switches and plugs that are visible; do not perform any electrical testing or remove any panels. Was a switch, plug or fuse off (and is it sorted), or does the socket work fine with something else?
The spur switch above the worktop is on and its little neon light is lit. Other sockets and lights in the kitchen work fine, and nothing's tripped at the consumer unit.

[Heading: Mains input / control]
Thank you for confirming that the socket and switch are working correctly. Since there are no lights at all despite power being present, the issue likely lies within the dishwasher’s mains input or control board. Please do not attempt to open the appliance yourself, as this requires specialist knowledge. An appliance engineer is the best next step to diagnose and repair this safely. I am not recommending any specific part for you to replace at this stage.
